Subject: Canopy Health — privacy & support access checklist

Hi Alyssa / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — the demo was great and we appreciated the detailed walk-through of Canopy's ingestion and patient lookup flows. As promised, I'm writing up the follow-up items we agreed to so your security and engineering teams can review. High-level asks below; see questions 1–6 and the attachments for a proposed initial checklist we can iterate on.

Quick summary (actionable items):
- We will provide a short support-access runbook and evidence package (SOC2 excerpts, audit logs) by EOD Wednesday.
- You asked for clarity on PII handling for both embeddings and logs — see Q1/Q2.
- We recommend a short sync between your infra/security and our solutions engineering to validate residency and break-glass workflows (proposed 04/07).

Questions for Canopy (short answers appreciated):
1) Data residency: Which customer or patient data must remain in-region (US-only)? Are there any state-specific restrictions?
2) PII classification: Do you consider patient identifiers (MRN, SSN, DOB) high risk for our processing path (i.e., must be redacted or tokenized before model input)?
3) Retention: What are your minimum log-retention requirements for support/troubleshooting logs vs. audit logs (e.g., 90 days vs. 7 years)?
4) Support access model: Do you require break-glass with two approvals, JIT ephemeral credentials, session recordings, or a combination?
5) Least-privilege roles: Any existing role names/IDs in your IAM we should map to (e.g., "SupportEngineer", "SRE", "ComplianceReader")?
6) Evidence: Please attach your compliance matrix or the specific questions you want our SOC2/controls deck to address.

Attachments: Canopy_Compliance_Matrix_Q1_2027.xlsx (placeholder), RWI_support_access_playbook_v2.pdf (attached by me).

Next steps I propose:
- You send quick responses to Q1–Q3 by EOD Tuesday.
- We run a 30-min technical sync with your infra (Karthik + Monica + your engineering lead) on 2027-04-07 at 10:00 PT to review access controls and residency.
- After that call we will produce a short technical note documenting: data flow (ingest → storage → model), RBAC mappings, break-glass steps, and recommended retention settings.

Thanks — happy to adjust the plan based on your priorities.

Best,

Logan Wright

Logan — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers inline below and attaching our compliance matrix (Canopy_Compliance_Matrix_Q1_2027.xlsx).

Q1) Residency: US-only for any PHI. We try to keep patient identifiable data within US regions; if you support multi-region routing we need the ability to opt out of non-US shards.

Q2) PII classification: Yes — MRN/SSN/DOB are high-risk. We prefer tokenization before model input for anything that leaves our control. Embeddings that could reconstruct identifiers need to be avoided unless hashed/salted.

Q3) Retention: Operational logs for support/team troubleshooting — 90 days. Audit logs (compliance/legal) — 7 years.

Q4) Support access: Break-glass requires two approvers (on-call manager + security) and JIT ephemeral credentials that expire after the session. Session recording and immutable audit logs are required for any session that touches PHI.

Q5) Roles: We have "canopy_support", "canopy_sre", "canopy_compliance_read" — happy to provide IAM role ARNs after the sync.

Q6) Evidence: Matrix attached. Would also like to review your SOC2 section on log collection and key rotation — could you point us to a short excerpt?

Thanks — Tom and I confirmed the 04/07 10:00 PT slot works. Please send calendar invite.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Chen

Logan / team — great context. I pulled together a concise set of responses and a proposed baseline configuration we can use as a starting point for the technical note. Attaching the RWI_support_access_playbook_v2.pdf for your reference (same as attachment Logan referenced).

Proposed baseline (short):
- Data residency: Host customer datasets in a single US region by default; provide region-locking flag per-tenant.
- PII handling: Default pipeline will redacted fields marked as HIGH_RISK in the ingest schema. For customers who require tokenization, we support a pre-ingest tokenization hook (customer-managed KMS recommended).
- Embeddings: We recommend only storing deterministic, salted hashes for IDs referenced by embeddings. No raw PII should be persisted with embeddings.
- Retention: Support/troubleshooting logs = 90 days (rolling); Audit logs = 7 years (archived, WORM-enabled).
- Support access: JIT ephemeral access via our bastion + short-lived role assumption. Break-glass flow: request → two approvers (manager + security) → temporary role issuance with mandatory session recording and immutable audit trail. Escalation to compliance for PHI exposure.
- Least privilege: Map our roles to your suggested names during the sync, e.g., "rwi_support" -> "canopy_support".

Open items we’ll confirm on the 04/07 call:
- Whether Canopy wants log copies shipped to a customer-owned S3 (preferred) or retained in our encrypted long-term store.
- The exact list of fields you want tokenized vs. redacted.
- Any state-specific residency rules (if CA has extra constraints).

Proposed deliverables after 04/07 call (timeline):
- 48 hours: technical note (data flow, RBAC mappings, break-glass steps).
- 5 business days: evidence package (SOC2 excerpts, sample audit logs, rotation policy).

If that looks good I’ll prepare the technical note template for our call. Karthik — can you also confirm the session-recording implementation and where logs are stored?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Product Security Lead | Redwood Inference
